_readme: Verdicts for audit:distances findings that have already been ruled on, mirroring
audits/identity-triage.json. Section 3 (non-alpine routes carrying a peak's area_id)
says of itself that it is a hypothesis, not a verdict -- so without this file the same
four rows get re-researched on every run.
Deleting an entry REOPENS the finding. Anything absent is NEW, and only new findings
count toward the closing line, so a real regression still stands out.
verdict: 'correct' = filed where it belongs, the filter is what is imprecise.
'deferred' = a genuine defect whose fix was consciously postponed.

misfiled.why: Genuinely misfiled. Its own overview places it 'about a mile in (clockwise) on the Silver Falls Loop Trail out of Ohanapecosh Campground, on the park's southeast side' and says outright it is 'unrelated to the park's glaciated alpine routes' -- yet it carries wa_mount_rainier, the SUMMIT area, roughly 15 miles away. Deferred rather than fixed because there is no destination: no Mount Rainier NP crag area exists, so this is a structural change (create area, reparent, let the route_count trigger settle), not a row edit.
misfiled.impact: Browsing Mount Rainier lists a V0 forest boulder among 20 glaciated routes.

misfiled.why: On the peak's own approach: 'a flat-topped erratic beside the White Chuck Glacier basin, climbed almost in passing by parties on Glacier Peak's standard south-side approach'. Filing it under Glacier Peak is right; discipline=bouldering is what trips the filter.

A 7-pitch, 700 ft, Grade III bolted alpine route up the southwest arete of Eros Tower, a rock sub-summit of Morning Star Peak. discipline=sport is accurate for the protection and is what trips the filter; the area is right.

The problem IS the summit block: 'a short, exposed boulder problem atop the true summit of Colchuck Balanced Rock -- climbing the balanced block itself'. dist_km 16.74 is the approach to the peak, not an incoherent boulder approach.
